chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:

I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar was brought forth, having drunk wine, and ʿUmar ordered that he be struck. But no one stepped forward against him to strike him, until ʿAlī عليه السلام stood up with a folded strap and struck him with it forty times.”

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar, the Imam Muḥammad al-Bāqir عليه السلام
key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ: forty; the number of lashes mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْخَمْرَ: wine; an intoxicating drink whose consumption is forbidden
key_terms.بِنِسْعَةٍ: with a strap or thong used for striking
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, who carried out the striking
key_terms.عُمَرُ: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, mentioned as ordering the punishment

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the punishment for drinking wine and the role of ʿAlī عليه السلام in carrying it out?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts an incident in which ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar was punished for drinking wine. It highlights the implementation of the prescribed penalty for intoxicants and the role of Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام in carrying it out when others hesitated.
